jordan: Heads-up — started sketching a 'harmonized safety lattice' approach for canary/A-B rollouts + automatic fallback. Want quick sanity-check before I escalate to RFC. TL;DR: combine a multi-signal scoring lattice + discrete fallback actions, where signals have hysteresis windows and signal-level TTLs.

mei: quick Q — what do you mean by "lattice" here? layering signals or prioritized buckets?

jordan: layering + partial ordering. Think of signals as axes (latency, error-rate, perf-regressions, quality drift). We map observed vectors into discrete cells with precomputed policy actions (scale down, divert, full fallback, patch route). Cells get cardinality limits to avoid explosion.

samir: sounds like a decision-table but with decay semantics? where hysteresis avoids flip-flopping?

jordan: exactly. Each cell has enter/exit thresholds and a min- dwell window. Also plan soft-failure budgets so we can degrade non-critical tenants before global fallback.

elena: can we reuse existing observer probes & rollout telemetry? I want to avoid another custom store for the lattice state.

jordan: yes — idea is to piggyback on observer-runner signals and the metric ingestion stream. Lattice state is ephemeral and reconstructable from latest signals + probe history; but we need a fast cache for signal aggregates.

mei: what about composition of fallback actions? e.g., start with routing diversion -> model-variant fallback -> full degrade. Are these orthogonal or encoded into the cell?

jordan: encoded into the cell as ordered action lists. Each action has a retry/backoff policy and an idempotent revert. That allows partial rollback if upstream conditions improve.

samir: how do we prevent noisy signals from triggering cascade? example: transient latency spike causing rapid routing changes -> kv cache thrash -> more latency.

jordan: a few mitigations: 1) signal smoothing (EWMA + outlier clipping), 2) action preconditions (only apply route diversion if model QPS > X), 3) local-circuit short-circuit for cache-sensitive actions. Also we keep a global rate limiter on action churn.

elena: operationally, who owns the cell->action mappings? product? infra? we need an audit trail.

jordan: propose ownership: infra defines primitives (divert, pin-variant, throttle, degrade-flags). Product defines default lattice policy per product line; each tenant can opt-in custom overrides via a policy manifest. All changes recorded in audit log and can be rolled back.

deploy-bot: canary build 2026.03.15_12:21 deployed to canary cluster 'shadow-arch-3' :rocket:

mei: for manifests — let's make them small JSONs with references to action templates, not full inline scripts. Also include a severity weight to help lattice ranking.

jordan: agreed. Templates + weight + conditions. Condition grammar probably biggest design task — needs expressivity for temporal windows, percentiles, and cross-signal tests.

samir: i worry about policy evals being on the hot path. Do we evaluate cell mapping upstream (edge) or centrally?


jelena: (typo) elena: central eval with local caching seems safer. We can push a compact decision token to edge that resolves rapidly.

jordan: implementation sketch: central evaluator consumes ingestion stream, updates lattice aggregates, emits decision tokens and action diffs to a control-plane pubsub. Edge agents subscribe to tokens and apply actions locally. Decision tokens include version + TTL + signature.

mei: what about debugability? need clear traces: which signal triggered what action, plus before/after routing table snapshots.

jordan: yes — every token emits a trace id; actions log provenance with sampling. Console will show a timeline and a reversible diff view.

elena: can we add a "probe backfill" step — when an action fires, spawn targeted probes to validate quality (synthetic prompts) so we can auto-unwind if we detect false positive?

jordan: love it. Backfill probes as a verification step that can accelerate revert if quality is unaffected. We'll weight that into the cell exit criteria.

samir: final ask — add a simulation harness to test lattice configs against historical telemetry before rollout.

jordan: on the list. I'll draft a short RFC with: 1) lattice model + data schema, 2) action primitives + templates, 3) control-plane token flow, 4) safety knobs (hysteresis, budgets, rate limits), 5) ops UX + tracing, 6) simulation plan.

mei: thumbs-up. ping me on the RFC when ready. :thumbsup:

elena: can I pair on the condition grammar?

jordan: yes, pls. I'll DM a rough proto.

samir: awesome. Thanks jordan, this lattice framing feels promising and distinct from our existing decision-plane models.
